description.description: Information regarding the process of 'vouching' for a voter's address at a polling place. The text explains that a registered voter from the same precinct can sign an oath confirming a person's address, and includes rules such as a limit of eight voters and a restriction against vouching for others if you were vouched for yourself. Portions of the text are highlighted in yellow and red.
description.ocrText:
③ Registered voter who can confirm your address

A registered voter from your precinct can go with you to the polling place to sign an oath confirming your address. This is known as 'vouching.' A registered voter can vouch for up to eight voters. You cannot vouch for others if someone vouched for you.
